content: tidepool: staging deploys from the release branch; main only runs CI.
ledgerline: refunds must be idempotent by request id. A retried refund with the same key returns the original response and never writes a second ledger entry.
ledgerline: the public API allows 100 requests per minute per merchant key, enforced by the tower layer in src/middleware/rate_limit.rs.
orchard: the warehouse is a single DuckDB file. Chose it over a Postgres warehouse because every consumer is a batch job on the same host and it needs no operations work.
beacon: wrap errors with fmt.Errorf and %w at every layer; the CLI prints only the outermost message unless --verbose is set.
tidepool: components use CSS modules colocated as Component.module.css; no styled-components in new code.
Task: add a partial-refund endpoint, POST /v1/payments/{id}/refunds, backed by a new refunds table. The handler goes in src/api/refunds.rs.
The IdempotencyLayer in src/api/payments.rs keys on the Idempotency-Key header and keeps keys in an in-process DashMap, so they vanish on every restart.

Command failed: cargo check -p ledgerline-api → error[E0599]: no method named `fetch_optional` found for struct `QueryAs<'_, Postgres, RefundRow, PgArguments>` in the current scope; note: there are multiple different versions of crate `sqlx_core` in the dependency graph
cargo tree -d shows two copies of sqlx-core: 0.7.4 pulled in by crates/ledger-core and 0.8.2 from the api crate.
Moved the dependency into [workspace.dependencies] at 0.8.2 and switched both crates to workspace = true. The whole workspace checks clean now.
Command failed: cargo test -p ledgerline-api refunds → thread 'refunds::partial_refund_roundtrip' panicked: error communicating with database: Connection refused (os error 61), 127.0.0.1:5432
The local compose stack had stopped when the laptop slept. Ran docker compose up -d db, waited for it to accept connections, and the suite passed: 14 tests.

Decided to persist idempotency keys in Postgres (table idempotency_keys, unique on merchant_id and key, 24-hour TTL swept hourly) instead of the in-process map: keys have to survive restarts and be shared by all three replicas.
Command failed: cargo sqlx prepare --check → error: query data in .sqlx is out of date for src/api/refunds.rs:88; run `cargo sqlx prepare` to update it
Regenerated the offline cache against the dev database and committed the three new JSON files; the CI job that builds without a database accepts it now.
Command failed: cargo test -p ledgerline-api refunds::over_refund_rejected → assertion `left == right` failed: expected status 422 Unprocessable Entity, got 500 Internal Server Error
The amount_cap_chk constraint violation was bubbling up as a generic database error. Mapped it to ApiError::Validation and the case passes.
Task: tests/e2e/checkout.spec.ts fails about one run in five on CI. Find the cause and make it reliable.
Command failed: npx playwright test tests/e2e/checkout.spec.ts --repeat-each=10 → 2 failed: Timeout 5000ms exceeded waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }) to be enabled
The button stays disabled until the shipping-rates request resolves, and on CI that request goes to the real staging rates service, which takes 3 to 7 seconds.
Stubbed the rates request with page.route() returning tests/fixtures/rates.json instead of raising the timeout; that spec isn't meant to exercise the rates service.
With the stub in place it passed 50 of 50 repeats locally and three CI runs in a row.
Next: wire the new PromoCode component into CartSummary.
Command failed: npx tsc --noEmit → src/components/cart/CartSummary.tsx(42,19): error TS2345: Argument of type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'.
Narrowed the value with an early return when it is missing, instead of a non-null assertion. Type check is clean.
Command failed: npm run build → [vite]: Rollup failed to resolve import '@tidepool/ui/tokens' from 'src/theme/index.ts'.
The UI package's exports map had no entry for that subpath. Added it in packages/ui/package.json and the production bundle comes out at 412 kB gzipped again.
Learned: flaky Playwright specs in tidepool have so far always come down to a live network call; open the trace's network tab before touching any timeout.
quillpad: Riverpod over Bloc, because providers compose without boilerplate event classes and code generation keeps them typed; the team already knew it from an earlier app.
Task: build a daily_sales_rollup DAG in orchard that reads the parquet drops in data/raw/sales/ and writes per-store aggregates into the warehouse DuckDB file.
Command failed: airflow dags test daily_sales_rollup 2026-01-19 → ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orchard.transforms'
The scheduler image installs requirements.txt but never installs the package itself, so only the dags/ folder ends up on the path.
Added pip install -e . after the requirements layer in the Dockerfile and rebuilt; the DAG run gets past its imports now.
Doing the aggregation as DuckDB SQL straight over the parquet files instead of in pandas: a pandas prototype of the same groupby peaked at 11 GB RSS on 41M rows.
Command failed: python -m orchard.jobs.rollup --days 92 → duckdb.OutOfMemoryException: Out of Memory Error: could not allocate block of size 256.0 KiB (3.7 GiB/3.7 GiB used)
Set DuckDB memory_limit to 4GB and temp_directory to /tmp/duckdb_spill so big aggregates spill to disk instead of dying.
Spilling made the 92-day run take 19 minutes, three times slower. Raised memory_limit to 8GB on the workers, which have 16 GB, and kept the spill directory as a safety net; the run is back to 6m40s.

Command failed: pytest tests/test_rollup.py → AssertionError: Attributes of DataFrame.iloc[:, 2] (column name='store_id') are different. Attribute 'dtype' are different: [left]: int64, [right]: object
Cast it to string when the loader reads the parquet, and the expected frame matches; 18 passed.
Learned: airflow dags test runs inside the scheduler image, so a package that imports fine in my venv can still be missing there.
ledgerline: money is always i64 minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code next to it; never f64, and never an amount without its currency.
orchard: every DAG task must be idempotent for its logical date: overwrite the partition, never append to it.
Task: add a `beacon sync` subcommand that pushes local probe configs to the remote registry, with --dry-run and --concurrency flags.
Subcommands live in cmd/beacon/, one file each, registered with the root command from init(); sync goes in cmd/beacon/sync.go.
Command failed: go vet ./... → cmd/beacon/sync.go:62:3: loopclosure: loop variable cfg captured by func literal
Bumped the go directive in go.mod from 1.21 to 1.22 so every iteration gets a fresh copy; the check is clean and the goroutine body is unchanged.

Command failed: go test -race ./internal/registry/... → WARNING: DATA RACE Write at 0x00c0001a4018 by goroutine 23: beacon/internal/registry.(*Client).recordResult() --- FAIL: TestPushConcurrent (0.31s)
Put the shared results slice behind a mutex; 200 repeated runs under the detector come back clean.
Default --concurrency to 4, not runtime.NumCPU(): the registry rate-limits each token to 5 concurrent requests and CI runners have 16 cores.
Then cut v0.4.0 with goreleaser, publishing darwin and linux archives for amd64 and arm64.
Command failed: goreleaser release --clean → ⨯ release failed after 3s error=yaml: unmarshal errors: line 14: field format not found in type config.Archive
The v2 schema takes a list there. Switched to the plural key with tar.gz, and a snapshot build produced all 4 archives.
Learned: run goreleaser check before tagging; it validates .goreleaser.yaml against the installed version's schema in under a second.
tidepool: chose TanStack Query over RTK Query for server state. Most screens are read-heavy lists, and RTK Query would bring in a Redux store we otherwise don't need.
beacon: config is TOML at ~/.config/beacon/config.toml. Chose TOML over YAML because probe definitions are flat tables, and YAML's implicit typing once turned a probe named no into false.
ledgerline: chose sqlx over Diesel because we want compile-time-checked raw SQL and native async; Diesel would need diesel-async and its own DSL for the settlement queries.
Task: add offline draft saving to quillpad's editor screen. Drafts must survive the app being killed and sync when the network comes back.
State is Riverpod 2.5 with riverpod_generator; the editor screen is driven by EditorController in lib/features/editor/editor_controller.dart.
Storing drafts in a drift (SQLite) table instead of shared_preferences: a draft can reach 200 KB of rich text, and the sync queue needs to query by updated_at.
Command failed: dart run build_runner build → [SEVERE] riverpod_generator on lib/features/editor/draft_provider.dart: Could not generate, the library is missing part 'draft_provider.g.dart'.
Added the missing part line at the top of the file and re-ran with --delete-conflicting-outputs; codegen produced 4 files.

Command failed: flutter run -d emulator-5554 → Execution failed for task ':app:checkDebugAarMetadata'. A dependency (work-runtime 2.9.0) requires libraries and applications that depend on it to compile against version 34 or later of the Android APIs; :app is currently compiled against android-33.
Raised compileSdk and targetSdk to 34 in android/app/build.gradle; the app installs and launches on the emulator now.
Command failed: flutter test test/editor/draft_sync_test.dart → Bad state: Tried to read the state of an uninitialized provider (draftSyncProvider).
Wrapped the pumped widget in a scope with an override for the connectivity stream; all 11 pass.
Sync triggers on connectivity changes plus a 15-minute WorkManager periodic task rather than a foreground timer, so drafts still sync after the app has been killed.
Command failed: flutter test integration_test/offline_draft_test.dart → SqliteException(1): no such table: drafts
Bumped schemaVersion to 2 with an onUpgrade step that creates it, so phones upgrading from 2.2 get it as well; the on-device run passes.
orchard: raw store feeds land in data/raw/sales/<date>/ as parquet, with a manifest.json written last once the drop is complete.
quillpad: one feature per folder under lib/features/<name>/, with data/, domain/ and presentation/ inside.
tidepool: Playwright traces are uploaded only on the first retry (trace: 'on-first-retry'), so download them from the failed CI attempt, not from the green rerun.
Task: move ledgerline's local and staging Postgres from 14 to 16 and get the integration suite green on 16.
docker-compose.yml pins postgres:14.10 and staging runs a managed 14.9 instance; sqlx 0.8.2 supports 16 with no code change.
Command failed: cargo test -p ledgerline-api --test integration → test settlement::nightly_rollup_order ... FAILED: expected first row for merchant m_002, found m_017
The query in src/settlement/rollup.rs has no ORDER BY. 14 happened to return rows in insertion order; 16 plans a parallel aggregate and does not.
Added an explicit sort on merchant_id, then currency. It passes on both versions now; it was only ever green by accident.
Local compose and staging now run postgres:16.2. Production stays on Postgres 14 until the March maintenance window, because the managed major upgrade needs a 20-minute write freeze.
Second task: failed merchant webhook deliveries retry forever on 5xx and are flooding the outbox table. Put a cap on them.
Capped webhook delivery at 5 attempts with exponential backoff (base 30 s, factor 2) in src/webhooks/dispatcher.rs; after the last attempt the event moves to the dead_letter table.
Command failed: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings → error: this `if` has identical blocks at src/webhooks/dispatcher.rs:142 (clippy::if_same_then_else)
Collapsed the two branches into one arm. Lint is clean and 22 tests pass.
Learned: Postgres 16 can return rows in a different order than 14 did for the same query, so any test asserting row order without ORDER BY is a latent failure.
Task: upgrade tidepool from Vite 5.4 to 6.0, then React 18.3 to 19.0, one at a time and keeping CI green.
Command failed: npm run dev → Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module node_modules/vite/dist/node/index.js from vite.config.cjs not supported.
Converted the config file to TypeScript with an ES default export; the dev server starts on 5173 again.
Vite 6 is in and the production bundle is 6% smaller, 388 kB gzipped. Moving on to React 19.
Command failed: npx tsc --noEmit → src/hooks/useCartForm.ts(18,30): error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 0. The call is useRef<HTMLInputElement>().
Passed an explicit initial value of null at all 7 call sites; tsc is clean.
Chose MSW over Playwright's page.route() for API mocking, so one set of handlers in src/mocks/handlers.ts serves both component and e2e tests; the page.route stubs had been copied into 9 specs.
Command failed: npx playwright test → 31 failed: [MSW] Failed to register the Service Worker: The script has an unsupported MIME type ('text/html').
Ran the msw init command with public/ as the target and committed the generated script; all 64 specs pass again.
Learned: React 19's ref typing changes only show up under tsc --noEmit, not in vite dev, so the type check has to run before an upgrade counts as done.
beacon: cobra's persistent pre-run hooks don't chain by default; set cobra.EnableTraverseRunHooks = true or child commands skip the root's hook.
orchard: under pandas copy-on-write, chained assignment silently does nothing; assign with .loc on the original frame.
Prefer cargo check over cargo build while iterating on ledgerline: check takes about 25 seconds, a full build about 4 minutes.
quillpad: the minimum Android SDK is 24.
Task: upgrade orchard's Airflow from 2.8.1 to 2.10.3 in the compose stack and the worker image.
Command failed: airflow db migrate → sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) connection to server at 'airflow-db' (172.18.0.3), port 5432 failed: Connection refused
The metadata Postgres container was still initialising: compose started the scheduler first because depends_on had no health condition.
Gave the database service a pg_isready healthcheck and put condition: service_healthy on the scheduler and webserver; the migrate step runs cleanly.
Airflow 2.10 deprecates schedule_interval; 14 DAGs still use it and log a RemovedInAirflow3Warning on every parse.
Renamed schedule_interval to schedule across all DAGs now rather than waiting for Airflow 3: it's a mechanical change and the warnings were drowning the scheduler log.
Command failed: pytest tests/ -W error → DeprecationWarning: DataFrameGroupBy.apply operated on the grouping columns. This behavior is deprecated (orchard/transforms/margins.py:57)
Passed include_groups=False and selected the value columns explicitly; the suite is green with warnings still treated as errors, 63 passed.
Also asked to make daily_sales_rollup retry on transient failures.
Set retries=3 with a retry_delay of 10 minutes and retry_exponential_backoff=True in the rollup DAG's default_args.
Learned: depends_on in compose only orders container start and never waits for readiness, so anything that needs the database needs a healthcheck condition.
tidepool: Playwright specs should prefer getByRole and getByLabel; use getByTestId only where an element has no accessible name.
beacon: the minimum supported Go version is 1.22, matching the go directive in go.mod.
Task: ship beacon through a Homebrew tap and add shell completion.

Publishing through our own tap repo, beacon-tools/homebrew-tap, via goreleaser's brews section rather than submitting to homebrew-core, which expects a track record of stable releases we don't have yet.
Task: upgrade quillpad to Flutter 3.27 and Dart 3.6, and get the iOS build working on the new Xcode.
Command failed: goreleaser release --clean → ⨯ brew: could not update tap: 403 Resource not accessible by integration
The release workflow's default token is scoped to the beacon repository and can't push to any other repo.

Command failed: cd ios && pod install → [!] CocoaPods could not find compatible versions for pod 'sqlite3_flutter_libs': Specs satisfying the dependency were found, but they required a higher minimum deployment target.
Raised platform :ios to 13.0 in the Podfile and in the Runner project settings; all 38 resolve cleanly now.
Created a fine-grained token limited to the tap repo with contents write, stored it as the TAP_TOKEN secret and passed it to the brews block; the formula commit landed.
Command failed: flutter analyze → info • 'withOpacity' is deprecated and shouldn't be used. Use .withValues() to avoid precision loss • lib/theme/colors.dart:22:31 (127 issues found)
Next: beacon completion zsh should complete probe names from the local config.
Left the 127 deprecation infos for a separate PR: CI's analyze step runs with --no-fatal-infos, so they don't block this upgrade.
Command failed: go test ./cmd/beacon/... → --- FAIL: TestCompletionProbeNames: got [] want [api-health db-latency]; ValidArgsFunction was never called
Command failed: flutter test test/editor/draft_sync_test.dart → Expected: <1> sync call, Actual: <2>; the connectivity listener fires twice on resume.
It was registered on the root command instead of the subcommand that takes the arguments; moving it there made both expected values come back.
Debounced it by 2 seconds and made draining the queue idempotent per draft id; the test now sees exactly one.
Dropping Windows from the build matrix for now: the probe runner talks over unix sockets and nobody has asked for it. It can come back once there is a named-pipe transport.
Moved the background periodic sync from every 15 minutes to every 30 after battery stats put it at 4% daily drain on a mid-range phone; sync on reconnect stays immediate.
Learned: cobra only consults ValidArgsFunction on the command that actually receives the positional arguments.
Learned: after a Flutter bump, run pod repo update before pod install, or CocoaPods resolves against a stale spec index.
Android release size went from 31.2 MB to 29.8 MB after the upgrade, mostly from better tree-shaking of icon fonts.
ledgerline: every handler returns ApiError, which renders as an RFC 7807 problem+json body; don't return a bare StatusCode from new routes.
orchard: uv replaces pip-tools for lockfiles. uv pip compile is about 20 times faster and the lock resolves identically on the macOS laptops and the Linux workers.
tidepool: feature flags are read once at boot from /config.json and never polled. A flag flip needs a page reload, which is fine because flags only change at deploy time.
beacon: table-driven tests with a t.Run per case; golden files live under testdata/ and are refreshed with -update.
quillpad: golden images differ between macOS and Linux font rendering, so CI generates and checks goldens only on the Linux runner.
Task: cut ledgerline production over to Postgres 16 in the 18 March maintenance window, then verify settlement.
Command failed: sqlx migrate run → error: while executing migration 20260301120000_add_refund_reason: error returned from database: permission denied for schema public
Since Postgres 15, CREATE on that schema is no longer granted to every role by default, and ledger_migrator relied on the old default.
Granted CREATE to ledger_migrator explicitly and added the grant to infra/sql/roles.sql so a rebuilt instance has it; the three pending files then applied cleanly.
Production is on Postgres 16.2 as of 09:47. Settlement totals match the pre-upgrade snapshot to the cent.
Second task: merchants say webhook retries give up while their own deploys are still rolling out. Revisit the backoff.

Raised webhook max attempts from 5 to 8, moved the backoff factor from 2 to 3 and added up to 20% jitter, with any single delay capped at 1 hour; a delivery now keeps trying for about 3 hours instead of under 10 minutes.
Command failed: cargo test -p ledgerline-api webhooks → test webhooks::backoff_schedule FAILED: expected delay <= 3600s, got 3840s at attempt 8
The cap was applied before the jitter instead of after it. Swapped the order and the whole module is green.
Learned: before any major Postgres upgrade, diff the default privileges on the public schema; the migrator role is the one that breaks.
orchard: SQL lives in orchard/sql/*.sql and is loaded by name; no inline SQL longer than one line in Python code.
Task: tidepool's e2e job takes 14 minutes on CI. Get it under 6 without dropping specs.
CI runs Playwright with workers: 1 because of an old comment about shared login state, and every spec logs in through the UI at about 4 seconds each.
Switched to storageState: a setup project logs in once and saves .auth/user.json, the specs reuse it, and CI workers went from 1 to 4.
Command failed: npx playwright test tests/e2e/orders.spec.ts → 3 failed: expect(getByTestId('order-number')).toHaveText('Order #1042'), received 'Order #0000'
The per-test page.route() override never fires: while the MSW service worker is registered it answers the request first, and Playwright's route never sees it.

Reversed February's choice for e2e: Playwright specs go back to page.route() with serviceWorkers: 'block', and MSW stays only for the Vitest component tests. Shared response fixtures live in src/mocks/data/ so nothing is copied twice.
Those three pass now, and the e2e job takes 5 min 20 s on CI, down from 14.
Command failed: npm ci → npm ERR! code EBADENGINE Unsupported engine: wanted node >=22.0.0 (current: 20.11.1) for @tidepool/ui@2.0.0
Bumped .nvmrc and the setup-node version in the CI workflow to 22.11; installs are clean.
Learned: while a mock service worker is registered, Playwright route handlers never see the request; block service workers in the e2e config or the stubs silently lie.
quillpad: rich text is stored as Quill Delta JSON, not HTML, so concurrent edits merge as operations during sync.
beacon: logs go to stderr as logfmt; stdout carries only command output so it can be piped into jq.
Task: backfill orchard's daily_sales_rollup for Q1 2026 now that the late store feed has arrived.

Command failed: airflow dags backfill daily_sales_rollup -s 2026-01-01 -e 2026-03-31 → duckdb.IOException: IO Error: Could not set lock on file 'warehouse/orchard.duckdb': Conflicting lock is held in /usr/local/bin/python3.11 (PID 4127)
Backfill runs several logical dates in parallel, and the warehouse file accepts only one writing process at a time, so concurrent days collide.
Capped it at one active run and one running task instance for this job only (max_active_runs=1, max_active_tis_per_dag=1) and re-ran it; all 90 days completed in 2h 05m.
Two store feeds arrive up to 6 hours late on Mondays; 3 retries 10 minutes apart give up long before they land.
Changed daily_sales_rollup retries from 3 to 6 with exponential backoff capped by a max_retry_delay of 2 hours, so a feed up to about 8 hours late still lands in the same run.
Added a FileSensor on the feed's manifest.json in mode='reschedule' so the worker slot is released while it waits.
Command failed: pytest tests/test_sensors.py → airflow.exceptions.AirflowSensorTimeout: Sensor has timed out; run duration of 600.12 seconds exceeds the specified timeout of 600.0.
The fixture wrote the manifest under the wrong partition date; pointing it at the logical date makes it pass in under a second.
Learned: DuckDB allows one writer process per database file, so any orchard job that can run concurrently must write to its own file or be serialised.
ledgerline: the per-merchant rate limit went from 100 to 300 requests per minute after the March load test; the burst allowance stays at 50.
quillpad: never call ref.read inside build(); use ref.watch in build and ref.read only in callbacks.
tidepool: staging now deploys from main on every merge; the release branch was retired this month.
orchard: the sales rollup must succeed by 06:00 local time; on-call is alerted if the DAG run hasn't succeeded by then.
beacon: releases are cut only from tags matching v*.*.*; goreleaser runs in the release workflow, never locally against main.
Task: bring Windows back into beacon's release for v0.6.0; two users asked for it in the tracker.
The probe runner now goes through a transport interface: unix sockets on darwin and linux, named pipes on windows. Windows amd64 is back in the release matrix from v0.6.0, reversing the March drop.
Command failed: GOOS=windows go build ./... → internal/runner/signals.go:12:2: undefined: syscall.SIGUSR1
Split the signal handling into a unix-only file behind a build constraint, with a no-op twin for the other platform; cross-compiling for all three targets works now.
Command failed: go test ./internal/runner/... on the windows runner → --- FAIL: TestPipeRoundTrip: dial pipe beacon-probe: All pipe instances are busy.
The listener was created with the default of a single instance. Raising it to 8 and closing each connection in a defer stopped the flakiness: 500 runs green.
The v0.6.0 release run took 4m10s and produced 6 archives, the Homebrew formula and a Scoop manifest.
Learned: anything that touches syscall signals in Go needs a build constraint before the first cross-compile, not after CI fails.
quillpad: crash-free sessions are at 99.6% on the 2.3.0 release; the top crash is a null draft id on cold start.
ledgerline: settlement now runs at 02:00 UTC instead of midnight so it no longer overlaps the partition maintenance job.
tidepool: the user wants small PRs, one concern each and under 400 changed lines.
orchard: stop committing sample parquet files to the repo; tests build their frames with the factories in tests/factories.py.
beacon: the registry answers 429 with a Retry-After in seconds, and the client honours it before applying its own backoff.
quillpad: release builds use --obfuscate with --split-debug-info=build/symbols, and the symbols are archived per version.
